specs.title: FR13-TC-11 [edge] a client-supplied total_amount is recomputed by the backend, not stored as sent

annotations.description: Closes OQ-06, flagged in HW02 as a concern but never tested. README FR-08 requires the backend to recompute the total from the cart; api_specification.md 4.3 lets the client supply it. The cart is filled through POST /api/cart with known prices, so the correct total is EXACTLY 150000*2 + 99000 = 399000, and the row submits 999999999 instead. Asserting the stored value equals 399000 - rather than merely differing from what was sent - is what makes this falsifiable: a build that stored any other wrong number, or clamped, would pass a not-equal check.

specs.title: FR13-API-07 [negative] an expired token is refused by the admin endpoint

annotations.description: TC-03 covers a token that is structurally invalid; this covers one that is correctly signed but past its expiry, which is a different code path in jwt.verify. The token is minted by the test with an `exp` in the past. NB the SUT issues tokens with NO exp claim at all (server.js:69 calls jwt.sign with no expiresIn), so this row asserts that expiry is honoured when present - it does not claim the SUT expires its own sessions.

specs.title: FR13-API-08 [positive] the admin orders payload carries the fields the revenue KPI depends on

annotations.description: Every revenue assertion in this suite reads `total_amount` and `status` off this payload, so a rename or a type change there would silently invalidate all of them. Asserts each row has a numeric id, a finite numeric total_amount and a status drawn from the five known values. This is the row that would have caught the scaffold's `order.total` mistake (gap analysis finding 15) at the contract rather than as a confusing revenue mismatch.
